questions.question:
If momentum is increased by \(20\%\), then kinetic energy increases by

[JEE Main 2022, 29 Jul (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
The kinetic energy is given by \(KE=\dfrac{p^2}{2m}\)

So, \(\Delta KE=\dfrac{2p\Delta p}{2m}=\dfrac{p\Delta p}{m}\)

\(\Rightarrow\;\dfrac{\Delta KE}{KE}=\dfrac{p\Delta p}{m}\times\dfrac{2m}{p^2}=\dfrac{2\Delta p}{p}\)

Since the momentum p increases by \(20\%\), so the final momentum becomes \(1.2\,p\).

Hence, \(KE_{final}=\dfrac{(1.2p)^2}{2m}=1.44\dfrac{p^2}{2m}=1.44\;KE\)

So, \(\%\) change in \(KE=44\%\).

questions.question:
If the solution curve of the differential equation \(\frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{x+y-2}{x-y}\) passes through the point \((2,1)\) and \((k+1,2), k>0\), then

 

[JEE Main 2022, 29 Jul (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
Given \( \frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{x+y-2}{x-y} \).

Put \(X=x-1\) and \(Y=y-1\).

Then \( \frac{dY}{dX}=\frac{X+Y}{X-Y} \).

Put \(Y=vX\), so \( \frac{dY}{dX}=v+X\frac{dv}{dX} \).

Therefore \( v+X\frac{dv}{dX}=\frac{1+v}{1-v} \).

So \( X\frac{dv}{dX}=\frac{1+v}{1-v}-v=\frac{1+v^2}{1-v} \).

Hence \( \frac{1-v}{1+v^2}dv=\frac{dX}{X} \).

Integrating, \( \tan^{-1}v-\frac{1}{2}\log_e(1+v^2)=\log_e X+C \).

Since the curve passes through \((2,1)\),

we have \(X=1\) and \(Y=0\), so \(v=0\).

Thus \(0=\log_e 1+C\), hence \(C=0\).

Therefore \( \tan^{-1}v-\frac{1}{2}\log_e(1+v^2)=\log_e X \).

Now the curve passes through \((k+1,2)\), so \(X=k\), \(Y=1\), and \(v=\frac{1}{k}\).

Hence \( \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{k}\right)-\frac{1}{2}\log_e\left(1+\frac{1}{k^2}\right)=\log_e k \).

 \( 2\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{k}\right)-\log_e\left(1+\frac{1}{k^2}\right)=2\log_e k \).

So \( 2\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{k}\right)=2\log_e k+\log_e\left(1+\frac{1}{k^2}\right) \).

Thus \( 2\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{k}\right)=\log_e k^2+\log_e\left(\frac{k^2+1}{k^2}\right) \).

Therefore \( 2\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{k}\right)=\log_e(k^2+1) \).

Let \( Q \) be the foot of perpendicular drawn from the point \( P(1,2,3) \) to the plane \( x+2 y+z=14 \). If \( R \) is a point on the plane such that \( \angle P R Q=60^{\circ} \), then the area of \( \triangle P Q R \) is equal to

\(S=1+4+3-14=-6\)

questions.question:
Bag \( I \) contains 3 red, 4 black and 3 white balls and Bag \( I I \) contains 2 red, 5 black and 2 white balls. One ball is transferred from Bag \( I \) to Bag \( I I \) and then a ball is drawn from Bag \( II \). The ball so drawn is found to be black in colour. Then the probability, that the transferred ball is red is:

 

[JEE Main 2022, 29 Jul (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
Let \(T_R\), \(T_B\) and \(T_W\) denote the events that the transferred ball is red, black and white, respectively, and let \(D_B\) denote the event that the ball drawn from Bag II is black.

\(\displaystyle P(T_R)=\dfrac{3}{10},\quad P(T_B)=\dfrac{4}{10},\quad P(T_W)=\dfrac{3}{10}\)

If a red ball is transferred, Bag II contains \(5\) black balls out of \(10\) balls.

\(\displaystyle P(D_B\mid T_R)=\dfrac{5}{10}\)

If a black ball is transferred, Bag II contains \(6\) black balls out of \(10\) balls.

\(\displaystyle P(D_B\mid T_B)=\dfrac{6}{10}\)

If a white ball is transferred, Bag II contains \(5\) black balls out of \(10\) balls.

\(\displaystyle P(D_B\mid T_W)=\dfrac{5}{10}\)

\(\displaystyle P(D_B)=\dfrac{3}{10}\cdot\dfrac{5}{10}+\dfrac{4}{10}\cdot\dfrac{6}{10}+\dfrac{3}{10}\cdot\dfrac{5}{10}\)

\(\displaystyle \Rightarrow P(D_B)=\dfrac{15+24+15}{100}=\dfrac{27}{50}\)

By Bayes' theorem,

\(\displaystyle P(T_R\mid D_B)=\dfrac{\dfrac{3}{10}\cdot\dfrac{5}{10}}{\dfrac{27}{50}}=\dfrac{5}{18}\)

The correct option is \(B\).

Let \(X=\left[\begin{array}{l}1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{array}\right]\) and \(A=\left[\begin{array}{ccc}-1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & -1\end{array}\right]\). For \(k \in N\), if \(X^{\prime} A^k X\) \(=33\), then \(k\) is equal to-------

 

[JEE Main 2022, 29 Jul (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
Let \(E\) be the matrix whose only non-zero entry is \(E_{13}=1\).

Direct multiplication gives

\(A^2=I+6E\).

Since \(E^2=0\), for every positive integer \(m\),

\(A^{2m}=(A^2)^m=(I+6E)^m\).

Using the binomial expansion and \(E^2=0\),

\((I+6E)^m=I+6mE\).

Therefore,

\(A^{2m}=I+6mE\).

Let \(X=(1,1,1)^T\).

Then \(X^TIX=3\)

and \(X^TEX=1\).

Hence \(X^TA^{2m}X=3+6m\).

For an odd power,

\(A^{2m+1}=A(I+6mE)=A+6mAE\).

Now \(X^TAX=10\)

and \(X^TAEX=-1\).

Therefore,

\(X^TA^{2m+1}X=10-6m\).

The equation

\(10-6m=33\)

has no non-negative integer solution.

For even powers,

\(3+6m=33\),

so \(m=5\).

Thus

\(k=2m=10\).

Therefore, \(k=10\).

If \( [t] \) denotes the greatest integer \( \leq t \), then number of points, at which the function

\(f(x)=4|2 x+3|+9\left[x+\frac{1}{2}\right]-12[x+20]\) is not differentiable in the open interval \( (-20,20) \), is

 

[JEE Main 2022, 29 Jul (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
The function is

\(f(x)=4|2x+3|+9\left[x+\dfrac12\right]-12[x+20]\).

The term \(\left[x+\dfrac12\right]\) changes its value whenever \(x+\dfrac12\) is an integer.

Therefore,

\(x=n-\dfrac12\),

where \(n\) is an integer.

In the interval \((-20,20)\), these half-integers are \(-19.5,-18.5,\ldots,18.5,19.5\).

Their number is \(40\).

At each such point, the term \(9\left[x+\dfrac12\right]\) has a jump of \(9\),

while \([x+20]\) does not jump because a half-integer is not an integer.

Hence, \(f\) is discontinuous and therefore not differentiable at all these \(40\) points.

The term \([x+20]\) changes its value whenever \(x+20\) is an integer, that is,

whenever \(x\) is an integer.

The integers in \((-20,20)\) are \(-19,-18,\ldots,18,19\).

Their number is \(39\).

At each integer, the term \(-12[x+20]\) has a non-zero jump,

while \(\left[x+\dfrac12\right]\) does not jump.

Hence, \(f\) is not differentiable at all these \(39\) points.

The term \(4|2x+3|\) has a corner at \(2x+3=0\),

so, \(x=-\dfrac32\).

This point is already included among the half-integers.

Therefore, it does not add a new point.

Since no integer is a half-integer, the two sets are disjoint.

Hence, the total number of points is \(40+39=79\).

questions.question:
If the tangent to the curve \( y=x^{3}-x^{2}+x \) at the point \( (a, b) \) is also tangent to the curve \( y=5 x^{2}+2 x-25 \) at the point (2, \( -1) \), then \( |2 a+9 b| \) is equal to ______.

 

[JEE Main 2022, 29 Jul (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
The second curve is \(y=5x^2+2x-25\).

At \(x=2\), its ordinate is

\(y=5(2)^2+2(2)-25=20+4-25=-1\).

Therefore, the point of contact on the second curve is \((2,-1)\).

Differentiate the second curve.

Its tangent slope is \(10x+2\).

At \(x=2\), the slope is \(10(2)+2=22\).

Hence the common tangent is \(y+1=22(x-2)\).

Therefore, the common tangent is \(y=22x-45\).

The first curve is \(y=x^3-x^2+x\).

Its derivative is \(3x^2-2x+1\).

At the point \((a,b)\),

the tangent slope must also be \(22\).

Thus \(3a^2-2a+1=22\).

Therefore, \(3a^2-2a-21=0\).

Factoring gives \((3a+7)(a-3)=0\).

Hence \(a=3\) or \(a=-\dfrac73\).

The point must also lie on the common tangent

\(y=22x-45\).

For \(a=3\), the first curve gives

\(b=27-9+3=21\).

The common tangent gives

\(b=22(3)-45=66-45=21\).

Therefore, \(a=3\) is valid.

For \(a=-\dfrac73\), the first curve gives

\(b=-\dfrac{343}{27}-\dfrac{49}{9}-\dfrac73=-\dfrac{553}{27}\).

The common tangent gives

\(b=22\left(-\dfrac73\right)-45=-\dfrac{289}{3}\).

These values are not equal,

so \(a=-\dfrac73\) is rejected.

Thus \((a,b)=(3,21)\).

Therefore, \(|2a+9b|=|2(3)+9(21)|=|6+189|=195\).

questions.question:
The number of natural numbers lying between \(1012\) and \(23421\) that can be formed using the digits \( 2,3,4,5,6 \) (repetition of digits is not allowed) and divisible by \(55\) is

 

[JEE Main 2022, 29 Jul (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
A number divisible by \(55\) must be divisible by both \(5\) and \(11\)

Since the available digits are \(2,3,4,5,6\),

the final digit must be \(5\)

First consider a four-digit number \(abc5\)

The divisibility rule for \(11\) gives \(a+c-(b+5)=0\)

because the possible difference cannot reach \(11\) in magnitude.

For \(b=2\), the condition \(a+c=7\)

gives \(3245\) and \(4235\)

For \(b=3\), the condition \(a+c=8\) gives

\(2365\) and \(6325\)

For \(b=4\), the condition \(a+c=9\) gives

\(3465\) and \(6435\)

For \(b=6\), the condition \(a+c=11\) has no solution using the remaining digits.

Thus, there are \(6\) valid four-digit numbers,

and all lie between \(1012\) and \(23421\)

A five-digit number using all the digits and ending in \(5\)

must begin with \(23\) to be below \(23421\)

The two possible beginnings give \(23465\) or \(23645\),

both greater than \(23421\)

Therefore, there is no valid five-digit number, and the required count is \(6\)

questions.question:
Let \(A B\) be a chord of length 12 of the circle \((x-2)^2+(y+1)^2=\frac{169}{4}\). If tangents drawn to the circle at points \(A\) and \(B\) intersect at the point \(P\), then five times the distance of point \(P\) from chord \(A B\) is equal to.

 

[JEE Main 2022, 29 Jul (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
The circle has centre \(C=(2,-1)\) and radius \(R=\dfrac{13}{2}\)

Let \(d\) be the perpendicular distance from \(C\) to chord \(AB\).

\(\because AB=12\),

\(\left(\dfrac{AB}{2}\right)^2+d^2=R^2\)

\(\Rightarrow 6^2+d^2=\left(\dfrac{13}{2}\right)^2\)

\(\Rightarrow d^2=\dfrac{169}{4}-36=\dfrac{25}{4}\)

\(\Rightarrow d=\dfrac{5}{2}\)

\(\because AB\) is the chord of contact from \(P\), the line joining the centre to \(P\) is perpendicular to \(AB\).

The two right triangles formed are similar, so \(CP\cdot d=R^2\)

\(\Rightarrow CP=\dfrac{R^2}{d}=\dfrac{\frac{169}{4}}{\frac{5}{2}}=\dfrac{169}{10}\)

The distance of \(P\) from chord \(AB\) is \(CP-d=\dfrac{169}{10}-\dfrac{25}{10}=\dfrac{72}{5}\)

Five times this distance is \(5\times\dfrac{72}{5}=72\)
